entries.title: Mister Monday
entries.author: Garth Nix
entries.text: Arthur Penhaligon survives an attack that should have killed him when a strange key, shaped like a clock hand, comes into his possession. His rescue draws creatures from another realm into his world, bringing a dangerous plague with them. To understand the key and stop Mister Monday from reclaiming it, Arthur enters a house that only he can see. This opening adventure in The Keys to the Kingdom turns an ordinary boy’s survival into a journey through an unfamiliar and threatening order.

entries.title: The marriage surrender
entries.author: Michelle Reid
entries.text: Joanna left Alessandro Bonetti two years ago, convinced that she could not give him the marriage he wanted. When she needs his help, she returns to a husband she still loves. Sandro agrees to intervene only if she resumes life as his wife. Their reunion brings the painful memories of their wedding night back into focus. Michelle Reid builds this romance around the secret Joanna has withheld and the difficult question of whether renewed intimacy can be accompanied by honesty.

entries.title: The Riddle-Master of Hed  (Riddle-Master #1)
entries.author: Patricia A. McKillip
entries.text: Morgon, the prince of Hed, comes from a quiet farming land but has an unusual talent for solving riddles. Three stars on his forehead point towards a mystery he cannot explain. When hostile powers begin to pursue him, he leaves home in search of the High One, accompanied by the harpist Deth. In a world where vanished knowledge survives in riddles and appearances can deceive, this first novel in the trilogy makes the search for identity part of the adventure.

entries.title: SPQR
entries.author: Mary Beard
entries.text: Mary Beard traces Rome’s transformation from a small settlement into a power stretching across the Mediterranean. Alongside wars and political struggles, she examines how Romans understood citizenship, slavery, migration and their own place in the world. The book covers roughly a thousand years, connecting the growth of the state with the lives and assumptions of its inhabitants. Beard also considers why Roman arguments about power and belonging remain part of modern political conversation, while questioning familiar stories about the ancient past.

entries.title: Wayward Son
entries.author: Rainbow Rowell
entries.text: Simon Snow has defeated his enemy, survived the war and found love, yet the promised happy ending has not arrived. Hoping that a change of scene will help, he sets off across the American West with Penny and Baz. Their road trip brings unfamiliar magic, dangerous encounters and new strains on their relationships. The sequel to Carry On follows what happens after a hero’s great task is finished, when friendship and love must contend with the damage left behind.

entries.title: Chain Letter
entries.author: Christopher Pike
entries.text: Alison dismisses a threatening chain letter until it becomes clear that its sender knows the secret she shares with six friends. The message refers to a crime in the California desert and demands that each member of the group carry out a dangerous task. Refusal appears to bring increasingly serious consequences. As fear spreads among the friends, they must decide what to reveal and whom to trust. Christopher Pike turns their shared silence into the starting point for a suspense story about guilt and coercion.

entries.title: The outsiders
entries.author: William Thorndike
entries.text: William Thorndike studies eight company leaders whose approach differs from the familiar image of the charismatic chief executive. His central concern is capital allocation: how managers decide where money should go, and how those decisions affect long-term value per share. The examples include Berkshire Hathaway, the Washington Post Company and Teledyne. Through these company histories, Thorndike argues for attention to cash flow, disciplined decisions and independent judgement. The book presents an interpretation of past business performance, rather than a promise of future investment results.
entries.identityNotes: Business nonfiction by William/Will Thorndike, not S. E. Hinton novel. Performance claims attributed and no returns promised.

entries.title: Open Water
entries.author: Caleb Azumah Nelson
entries.text: A photographer and a dancer meet in a London pub and gradually fall in love. Both are young Black British artists, familiar with the discomfort of moving through institutions that welcome their talent without always making room for them as people. Their growing intimacy offers a place of safety, but fear and violence intrude on the relationship. Caleb Azumah Nelson’s novel explores the difficulty of being vulnerable when the surrounding world demands strength, linking romantic love with art, race and masculinity.

entries.title: Untamed

entries.text: Keilly is determined to resist Rod Bartlett’s charm. She believes he hurt her cousin Kathy and sees his attentions as part of a familiar pattern of attraction and abandonment. As her feelings change, Keilly struggles to decide whether to trust her own experience or her earlier judgement. Carole Mortimer’s romance follows the tension between suspicion, loyalty to family and the wish to believe that affection is sincere.

entries.title: Het gevaar van de joodse erfenis
entries.author: H. M. Reijzer
entries.text: Hans Reijzer onderzoekt hoe de psychoanalytische beweging is omgegaan met haar Joodse achtergrond en met antisemitische beeldvorming. Vanaf Freud speelt de angst om als buitenstaander te worden gezien een rol in de geschiedenis die hij beschrijft. Reijzer volgt discussies, ontmoetingen en conflicten binnen internationale psychoanalytische kringen. De titel verwijst naar de manier waarop betrokkenen hun erfenis als bedreigend konden ervaren. Het boek biedt daarmee een kritische geschiedenis van identiteit en uitsluiting binnen een wetenschappelijke en professionele beweging.

entries.title: Child neglect
entries.author: Janet Anne Basarab-Horwath
entries.text: Jan Horwath examines why child neglect can be difficult for professionals to recognise and assess. The book considers the causes and effects of neglect alongside the personal assumptions, working practices and organisational conditions that shape a response. Research evidence is brought into discussion with the dilemmas encountered by practitioners. A recurring concern is how different services can work together effectively. This study is intended to support reflection on professional assessment, with attention to the factors that can otherwise leave a child’s needs overlooked.

entries.title: Activiteit en begrip
entries.author: B. van Oers
entries.text: Bert van Oers onderzoekt in dit proefschrift hoe onderwijs vanuit de handelingspsychologie kan worden begrepen en verbeterd. Hij vertrekt vanuit de theoretische traditie van onder anderen Leont’ev en werkt uit wat activiteit betekent voor leren en begripsvorming. Daarbij staat ook de verhouding tussen theorie, onderzoek en onderwijspraktijk ter discussie. Het boek ontwikkelt een psychologisch-didactische benadering en maakt de aannames daarvan expliciet. Zo richt het zich op de grondslagen van onderwijs, met begripsontwikkeling als belangrijk vraagstuk.

entries.title: Bergje
entries.author: Bregje Hofstede
entries.text: Bregje Hofstede keert terug naar de Sass Songher in de Dolomieten, de berg die tijdens haar jeugd een bijna mythische betekenis kreeg. Eerst wandelt ze er met haar geliefde door de sneeuw, later komt ze alleen terug in de zomerhitte. Het landschap roept vragen op over wat herinneringen bewaren en wat een ander daarvan kan zien. Tijdens de tochten verbindt Hofstede haar eigen leven met gedachten over eenzaamheid, moederschap, toerisme en natuurbehoud. Wandelen wordt zo een manier om vroegere en huidige ervaringen naast elkaar te leggen.

entries.title: Out of my mind
entries.author: Sharon M. Draper
entries.text: Eleven-year-old Melody has cerebral palsy and cannot communicate through speech, but she notices and remembers far more than the people around her realise. A communication device gives her a new way to express what she knows. At school, that opportunity exposes both her abilities and the assumptions her classmates and teachers have made about her. Told from Melody’s perspective, Sharon M. Draper’s novel explores friendship, exclusion and the difference between being able to speak and being willing to listen.

entries.title: Anne of Avonlea
entries.author: Lucy Maud Montgomery
entries.text: Anne Shirley begins teaching in Avonlea at sixteen, bringing her imagination and high expectations into a classroom that does not always behave as she hopes. New responsibilities at Green Gables and encounters with neighbours test the patience behind her good intentions. Familiar friendships continue to change as she moves towards adulthood. This sequel to Anne of Green Gables follows the gap between Anne’s ideals and daily life, finding humour and affection in her attempts to help others while learning more about herself.

entries.title: Het zingende gras
entries.author: Doris Lessing
entries.text: Mary Turner verruilt haar leven in de stad voor een huwelijk met een weinig succesvolle boer in Zuid-Rhodesië. Op de afgelegen boerderij raken armoede, hitte en eenzaamheid verweven met de spanning tussen haar en haar man. Haar omgang met de zwarte bediende Mozes wordt bepaald door een koloniale samenleving waarin raciale ongelijkheid de verhoudingen beheerst. Doris Lessing onderzoekt in deze roman hoe persoonlijke afhankelijkheid en maatschappelijke machtsverschillen elkaar versterken. Het verhaal plaatst het vastgelopen huwelijk binnen de gewelddadige orde die het omringt.

entries.title: De droom van de Ier
entries.author: Mario Vargas Llosa
entries.text: Roger Casement onderzoekt als Brits diplomaat het geweld van koloniale machthebbers in Congo en het Amazonegebied. Deze historische roman volgt zowel zijn inzet voor onderdrukte mensen als de tegenstrijdigheden die zijn nalatenschap hebben bepaald.

entries.title: Perfume
entries.author: Patrick Süskind
entries.text: Jean-Baptiste Grenouille grows up in eighteenth-century France with an extraordinary sense of smell. Through Grenouille’s pursuit, it explores the connection between artistic mastery, possession and a disregard for other human lives.

entries.title: Monster

entries.text: Sixteen-year-old Steve Harmon is on trial for his alleged involvement in a robbery that ended in murder. Walter Dean Myers uses this unusual narrative form to explore identity, responsibility and the uncertainty of a young person facing judgement.

entries.title: An American Plague
entries.author: Jim Murphy
entries.text: Jim Murphy reconstructs the yellow fever epidemic that struck Philadelphia in 1793, when the city served as the temporary capital of the United States. Fear drove residents away, disrupted government and exposed sharp disagreements about how the disease should be treated. Drawing on historical accounts, the book follows the people who fled, those who remained and the efforts to care for the sick. Written for younger readers, it connects the medical uncertainty of the period with the social and political pressures of a city in crisis.

selection.method: Fresh 1000-row CNI and performance captures; live audit of all 164 eligible localized canonical sitemap pages. This is a defect-led editorial selection, not a whole-site traffic ranking. Other missing pages need separate identity/source research.
